title: Efficacy of FLUOXETINE in children with drug-resistant, complex and rare epilepsy (FLUOXEPIL)
official: Randomized double-blinded placebo-controlled study of the efficacy of fluoxetine in add-on treatment of drug-resistant, complex and rare epilepsy in children aged 8 years and older: use of a design evaluating the time to reach a defined number of seizures for each child during the prospective observational phase (FLUOXEPIL)
summary: Main objective: To compare the efficacy of fluoxetine plus anti-seizure treatment as usual (TAU) versus placebo plus TAU in reducing the frequency of seizures in children of at least 8 years of age having drug-resistant epilepsy.
conditions: complex and rare epilepsy in children aged 8 years and older

interventions.name: Cellulose microcristalline (matière première à usage pharmaceutique)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Signed and dated informed consent form by the two parents (or one, if single-parent family, as documented in the medical file).
2. Patient for whom at least 4 treatments (anti-seizure medications) have been prescribed, alone or in combination, at appropriate dosage, without controlling the seizures.
3. Patient exhibiting daytime seizures with loss consciousness and/or leading to falls, and/or cyanotic nocturnal seizures
4. Patient presenting at least 3 seizures/months on average
5. Less than five concomitant anti-seizure medications (ASMs) at time of inclusion
6. Patient having a dose of ASMs which is stable for at least one week prior to screening.
7. For girls of childbearing potential, willing to use a highly effective contraceptive method throughout the study and until 6 weeks after the end of the treatment.
8. Patient with no indication or epilepsy surgery, contra-indication of the surgery or failure/refusal of epilepsy surgery
9. Patient having the ability to take oral medication
10. Patient who is a beneficiary of or affiliated to a social security scheme
11. Documented willingness of both parents to comply with all study procedures for the duration of the study (or one if single-parent  family)
12. Child or adolescent aged of 8 – 17 years old.
13. Child assent for his/her participation to the research
14. Patient with rare / complex epilepsy: Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy, structural severe epilepsies, rare epileptic syndromes as defined by the International League Against Epilepsy
15. Patient presenting drug-resistant focal or generalized epilepsy according to the ILAE definition.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patient participating to another clinical trial
2. Patient not in capacity to consent and/or without legal representative present to receive the information and give consent for the patient’s participation
3. Patient with known QT prolongation.
4. Patient with previous history of mania/hypomania.
5. Patient taking oral anticoagulants.
6. Patient with a history of bleeding disorders.
7. Patient having a known history of diabete(s).
8. Patient presenting with galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption syndrome
9. Pregnant or breastfeeding women
10. Patient under 20 kg at the screening visit
11. Concomitant use of monoamin oxidase inhibitor or metoprolol
12. Patient with history or presenting any abnormality of renal, hepatic or cardiac function
13. Patient with treated or untreated hypertension
14. Patient having a score of 23 or more obtained with the Neurological Disorders Depression Inventory-Epilepsy for Youth scale or any suicidal idea
15. Patient presenting contraindications to fluoxetine: hypersensitivity to fluoxetine and/or excipients
16. Patient with limited French proficiency
